reason: Abstract explicitly reports FBN1 mutations in patients screened for marfanoid habitus and intellectual disability, including four pathogenic FBN1 mutations and chromosomal rearrangements. Directly on-topic for the FBN1 gene collection.

Abstract directly addresses FBN1 variant interpretation, co-occurrence of FBN1/FBN2 variants in fibrillinopathies, and challenges in variant classification for Marfan syndrome and congenital contractural arachnodactyly. Core FBN1 genetics content.

Title and abstract describe reduced penetrance of a specific FBN1 mutation (R2726W) in Marfan syndrome, with direct clinical implications for genetic counselling. Squarely on-topic for the FBN1 gene collection.

Title explicitly names a novel FBN1 mutation causing geleophysic dysplasia. FBN1 mutations are known to cause multiple fibrillinopathy phenotypes beyond classic Marfan syndrome. Directly on-topic for the FBN1 gene collection.

Study classifies Marfan patients by FBN1 mutation type (haploinsufficient vs. dominant negative) and assesses differential therapeutic response to losartan. FBN1 mutation classification is central to the paper's design and conclusions.

Novel FBN1 missense mutation (c.1708 T>G, p.C570G) in autosomal dominant Marfan syndrome; abstract explicitly states that ophthalmologic examinations were performed in affected family members. Directly on-topic for the FBN1 gene collection.

Title describes NGS screening for pathogenic mutations in 123 patients with Marfan syndrome or a related disease; FBN1 is the principal gene screened in this population. Abstract is absent but title is unambiguous.
Abstract reports 9 novel FBN1 mutations in German Marfan syndrome patients, characterising missense and frameshift variants across multiple exons. Classic FBN1 mutation discovery paper.

Paper directly studies SOX2 and its DBD-flanking region, showing how SOX2's positively-charged DFR enhances target search efficiency, 1D sliding on DNA, and nucleosome engagement (pioneering activity). SOX2 is both the principal subject and a mechanistically studied molecule. Fundamental SOX2 biology is within scope of a gene-centric ophthalmogenetics collection for SOX2.

Title describes an integrated clinical and molecular study of Turkish patients with Marfan syndrome and FBN1 variants, including novel variants. Abstract is absent but the title is unambiguous and directly on-topic for the FBN1 collection.

Abstract characterises a large FBN1 deletion CNV in a Marfan syndrome patient, proposes MMBIR as the formation mechanism, and places findings in the context of the ~2-7% of MFS caused by CNVs. Directly on-topic for FBN1 mutation mechanisms.

Abstract describes a GC-E (retGC1/GUCY2D) knockout mouse model that develops cone-specific dystrophy and paradoxical rod behaviour. This is a foundational paper for GUCY2D (Leber congenital amaurosis gene) and cone dystrophy, directly relevant to multiple genes in the multi-gene query (GUCY2D, GUCA1A, GUCA1B, CNGA1, SLC24A1).

Title 'Macular Dystrophy of the Cornea' is the principal clinical phenotype caused by CHST6 mutations. Even with an absent abstract, the title alone is sufficient to establish direct relevance to the CHST6 gene collection.

Title describes optic nerve hypoplasia/dysplasia in Coffin-Siris syndrome, which is caused by ARID1B mutations. This paper directly documents an ophthalmic structural manifestation of ARID1B-related disease, squarely within scope for an ophthalmogenetics collection.

Review covers calcium regulation in rod and cone photoreceptors, explicitly discussing the roles of CNGA1 (CNG channel) and SLC24A1 (NCKX exchanger) in calcium entry and extrusion in the outer segment. These two genes from the multi-gene query are central mechanistic subjects of the review.

Abstract reports peripapillary RNFL thickness measurements via SD-OCT in 29 eyes of 16 choroideremia (CHM gene) patients, documenting structural defects. Directly characterises retinal pathology in CHM disease.

Title describes linkage analysis of choroideremia using physically mapped DNA markers. Even with an absent abstract, this is clearly foundational gene-mapping work for the CHM locus, directly on-topic for the CHM gene collection.

Abstract directly investigates deamidation of betaA3-crystallin (CRYBA1) and shows that specific deamidation sites trigger aggregation and alter interactions with the betaB1 subunit, linking to cataract pathogenesis. Directly on-topic for the CRYBA1 gene collection.

Classic 1974 electrophysiology paper establishing that the photoreceptor potential is generated by a light-induced decrease in Na+ conductance and demonstrating that extracellular Ca2+ mimics steady background illumination. These are foundational findings for the phototransduction cascade and visual physiology topic covered by this collection.

Abstract validates the laser speckle method against hydrogen clearance for measuring optic nerve head blood flow in rabbits, demonstrating responses to CO2 and endothelin-1. Directly on-topic for the ocular vascular physiology collection, covering retinal/ONH blood flow regulation mechanisms.
